title: Repeat Until the Condition Changes
content:
What problem does this solve?
A for loop is ideal when you already know the collection or range to visit. Dispatch sometimes repeats while a condition stays true — fuel remains, a warning is active, or an index has not reached the end. A while loop keeps going until that condition becomes false.

Previously in your program
You used for item in supplies and for i in range(len(party)). Those patterns still matter. while is for repetition that ends when something you update finally makes the condition false.

Basic syntax
  charge = 4
  while charge > 1:
      charge -= 1
  print(charge)

What actually happens
Python checks the condition before each pass. If it is true, the body runs. The body must make progress — update a counter, shrink a value, or advance an index — so the condition can become false. Without an update, the loop can run forever. Basilisk stops runaway code with a timeout; that message is feedback about missing termination, not a mystery crash.

When this is useful
Prefer for when visiting a known collection. Prefer while when you repeat until a changing condition says stop.
concepts: for processes a known collection or range
while repeats while a condition remains true
The loop body must update something toward termination
A missing update can create an infinite loop; timeouts are feedback

examples.title: Count down a charge
examples.explanation: Each pass reduces charge. When charge is no longer greater than 1, the loop ends and print shows what remains.

examples.title: Advance an index
examples.code:
readings = [5, 1, 2]
index = 0
seen = 0
while index < len(readings):
    seen += 1
    index += 1
print(seen)
examples.explanation: index advances each pass so the loop eventually stops. Prefer for when you only need each value; this shows while with len and indexing.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to update the variable the condition depends on
Using while when a plain for over the list would be clearer
Using sum() when the lesson asks you to accumulate with while
Putting the terminating update outside the loop body

exercises.title: Fuel reaches zero
hints: Trace fuel before each condition check.
The loop body subtracts 1 until fuel is no longer greater than 0.
When the loop ends, fuel is 0.

exercises.title: Make progress
exercises.prompt: Complete the loop body so distance moves toward zero and the while loop can finish. The program should print how many steps were taken.
exercises.starter_code:
steps = 0
distance = 3

while distance > 0:
    steps += 1
    ______

print(steps)

tests.message: Keep a real while loop whose condition can actually run and then change — not while False or a comparison that never runs.

tests.name: distance
tests.message: Update distance inside the while loop so the condition can become false.
Print the steps variable — do not hardcode the number of steps.

tests.name: steps
tests.message: Do not assign a fixed number to steps after the while loop — print the value the loop computed.
Print the number of steps taken (the final value of steps).

exercises.title: The signal never changes
exercises.prompt: This loop prints forever because signal never changes. Update signal inside the while loop so it prints 3, then 2, then 1, then clear.
hints: Print the current signal, then reduce it.
Inside the loop: print(signal), then signal -= 1.

tests.message: Keep a real while loop whose condition can actually run and then change — not while False or a comparison that never runs.

tests.name: signal
tests.message: Change signal inside the while loop body.

tests.name: print
tests.message: Print signal from inside the while loop body.
Print 3, then 2, then 1 from the loop, then clear.

exercises.title: for or while?
exercises.prompt: You must repeat a route check while a warning remains active. The number of checks is not known in advance. Which approach fits?
choices: A while loop, because repetition ends when the condition changes
A for loop over a fixed list, because all repetition should use for
exercises.success_message: Yes — when you stop because a condition changes, while matches the problem.
exercises.failure_message: Ask whether you already know every pass in advance, or whether you stop when a condition finally becomes false.
hints: The stopping rule is a changing condition, not a fixed collection length.
for shines when the sequence is already known.

exercises.title: Total the trail
exercises.prompt:
Write trail_total(distances) that returns the sum of the numbers in distances.

Use index = 0, total = 0, while index < len(distances), read distances[index], update the index, and return total. Do not use sum().
hints: Start index and total at 0 before the loop.
While index is still in range, add distances[index] to total, then increase index.
return total after the loop ends.

tests.message: Inside trail_total, use a while loop whose condition can actually run and then change — not a comparison that never runs.

tests.name: sum
tests.message: Do not call sum() — accumulate the total with your while loop.
Use while to total the distances — do not replace the while work with a for loop.
Do not call trail_total from inside itself — accumulate with your while loop.

tests.name: total
tests.message: Update total inside the while loop body as you visit each distance.

tests.name: index
tests.message: Update index inside the while loop so the loop can finish.
Use len(distances) in the while condition.

tests.name: distances
tests.message: Read values with distances[index] inside trail_total.
trail_total([]) should return 0.
trail_total([7]) should return 7.
trail_total([2, 3, 4]) should return 9.
trail_total([0, 5]) should return 5.
trail_total must generalize beyond a few fixed lists.
